### Colonies, relocation and losses

Removing your last ship from a planet immediately loses that colony. Returning ships must go to **existing** colonies, not abandoned planets; if no colony can receive a required relocation, those ships go to warp unless an explicit exception applies. You still defend an empty home planet with zero ships. Extra ship losses normally let the losing player choose their ships, unless the effect specifies someone else. A requirement to lose ships outside the encounter cannot be paid with encounter ships; if you have no eligible ships, lose none. Likewise you cannot activate a sacrifice requiring an outside ship by substituting an inside ship. Forced losses/sacrifices normally choose ships you control, not ships already in warp, removed or captured.

“Losing ships” are encounter participants that should suffer defeat's loss; ships “lost to warp” actually reach it involuntarily at some point in the encounter. “Sent” ships reach the warp through a specific action or effect, sometimes voluntarily, while not directly involved in the encounter; they count as lost rather than encounter-losing ships. An interruption preventing warp arrival means no actual warp loss. These distinctions matter for compensation, Healer, Observer, Void and Zombie.

evidence.text:
### Card information, discards and exhaustion

Hand size is public; card faces are private unless an effect says otherwise. You may make claims or lie about your hand during ordinary public table talk, but cannot show it; Mind has an additional secrecy restriction and deal terms must be honored. Table talk is public unless an effect permits secrecy. Discards are faceup and public, including all cards discarded together. When discard order matters, discard non-encounter cards first in alphabetical/numerical order, then encounter cards starting with offense clockwise and ending with defense, whose encounter card is on top.

Old terminology: challenge means encounter; cone means hyperspace gate. An unqualified deck or discard pile means the cosmic deck or its discard. A legal encounter is one where offense can ultimately gain a foreign colony without having to make a deal.

Ships landing on colonies do so simultaneously, including ships released by Mobius Tubes (FAQ p19, general landing rule). With Mobius Tubes and no colony to receive released ships, return those ships to warp; offense may first place up to four of its released ships in the gate.

Base card types are **attack, negotiate, Morph, reinforcement, flare and artifact**; encounter is a category, not one card type. Card-type costs such as Hate or Plague distinguish those six. No expansion card types are in scope.

If the cosmic deck runs out, reshuffle available discards. If a needed draw has no deck or discards, a **Cosmic Quake** makes everyone discard their hands; shuffle and deal eight to each player. If still insufficient, **Cosmic Aftershock** gathers all cosmic cards, including Miser's hoard and other set-aside cards, shuffles them, and replenishes Game Setup card holdings as at setup (including Miser's hoard). This is a needed-draw exhaustion rule, not an optional hand refresh.

### Start Turn and hand replacement

Start Turn occurs only before the first encounter of your turn, before Regroup effects. If offense has no encounter cards, reveal and discard the remaining hand, then draw eight new cards. You may first play legally playable non-encounter cards but are not required to play them. Hate draws a needed starting hand before using its power.

At Planning, a defense lacking encounter cards reveals/discards the remainder and draws eight cards, repeating until it has an encounter card. An offense that runs out later in its turn **when it needs to play an encounter card** ends its turn instead of drawing a replacement. Offense returns its committed ships to its own colonies; each ally returns that ally's committed ships to that ally's own colonies. The normal no-colony relocation rule applies. There is no automatic draw at the end of an encounter or turn, or merely for running out of cards. Alien and card effects can grant different draws.

### Card information, discards and exhaustion

Hand size is public; card faces are private unless an effect says otherwise. You may make claims or lie about your hand during ordinary public table talk, but cannot show it; Mind has an additional secrecy restriction and deal terms must be honored. Table talk is public unless an effect permits secrecy. Discards are faceup and public, including all cards discarded together. When discard order matters, discard non-encounter cards first in alphabetical/numerical order, then encounter cards starting with offense clockwise and ending with defense, whose encounter card is on top.

Old terminology: challenge means encounter; cone means hyperspace gate. An unqualified deck or discard pile means the cosmic deck or its discard. A legal encounter is one where offense can ultimately gain a foreign colony without having to make a deal.

Ships landing on colonies do so simultaneously, including ships released by Mobius Tubes (FAQ p19, general landing rule). With Mobius Tubes and no colony to receive released ships, return those ships to warp; offense may first place up to four of its released ships in the gate.

Base card types are **attack, negotiate, Morph, reinforcement, flare and artifact**; encounter is a category, not one card type. Card-type costs such as Hate or Plague distinguish those six. No expansion card types are in scope.

If still insufficient, **Cosmic Aftershock** gathers all cosmic cards, including Miser's hoard and other set-aside cards, shuffles them, and replenishes Game Setup card holdings as at setup (including Miser's hoard). This is a needed-draw exhaustion rule, not an optional hand refresh.

### Negotiate against negotiate: making a deal

Both sides' allies return ships to their own colonies, gain nothing and cannot participate in the deal. The main players have **one minute**. They may transfer cards from their hands and/or each grant the other **one colony on a planet where the giver already has a colony**, including a foreign colony. The recipient can use any own ships not in the warp. Existing ships coexist; the giver need not vacate, and vacating would eliminate the colony being offered. Return any remaining gate ships to offense's colonies.

A successful deal must actually transfer at least one card or colony; it may be one-sided. You cannot agree to do nothing. Tangible terms are restricted to permitted cards/colonies and specific power/card exceptions such as Zombie's liberation; future promises are unenforceable. Card terms may be explicit or vague but must be truthful and honored (if you promise your highest attack, give it). If time expires without agreement, **each main player loses three ships of their choice to the warp**, and offense cannot take an ordinary second encounter. Successful deals qualify for an ordinary second encounter but do not trigger win-only powers.

### Start Turn and hand replacement

Start Turn occurs only before the first encounter of your turn, before Regroup effects. If offense has no encounter cards, reveal and discard the remaining hand, then draw eight new cards. You may first play legally playable non-encounter cards but are not required to play them. Hate draws a needed starting hand before using its power.

At Planning, a defense lacking encounter cards reveals/discards the remainder and draws eight cards, repeating until it has an encounter card. An offense that runs out later in its turn **when it needs to play an encounter card** ends its turn instead of drawing a replacement. Offense returns its committed ships to its own colonies; each ally returns that ally's committed ships to that ally's own colonies. The normal no-colony relocation rule applies. There is no automatic draw at the end of an encounter or turn, or merely for running out of cards. Alien and card effects can grant different draws.

evidence.heading: Flare system
evidence.text:
### Flare system

Flares are not encounter cards. Each has printed Wild and Super effects, usage roles and timing. Normally use Wild; if it is your own alien's flare and your power is available, **you must use Super**, not choose Wild. If your power is lost or zapped, you can use only Wild until your power returns.

Return a flare to hand **immediately after its effect finishes**, rather than discard it, unless its effect states otherwise. A player may play **at most one flare per encounter**, and an individual flare can be used **only once per encounter even if it changes hands**. A Card Zap targeting the flare counts against the player's limit. Prevention of play differs from cancellation after play: see Anti-Matter's FAQ exception. If a Super enables a power use, that power can still be Cosmic Zapped even outside its usual role/phase. The flare remains in hand rather than being discarded or forced to Wild; Only Wild is available for an otherwise legal play while the power is zapped. Zapping the enabled power does not undo the already-played flare or permit a second play of it in the same encounter; the ordinary per-player and per-flare limits still apply. When your own Wild would otherwise be handed to your alien, keep it after resolution.

The FAQ quotes these Super effect timing clauses; they do not make a flare apply automatically in later encounters. Follow the full card for its other conditions and legal play.

| Original Super flare | Quoted effect timing |
|---|---|
| Kamikaze, Machine, Masochist | During each of **your own Regroup phases** |
| Miser | At the start of each of **your encounters** |
| Cudgel | Whenever you **use your power** |

These are effect timing clauses, not a reconstruction of an earlier permitted faceup-placement window (FAQ pp12,16–18).
